one-check-per-line.why: all 7 lines quoted in order, checks numbered 1 to 7

no-restated-rules.why: no branch, base, branch-name rule or return mechanics named

builder-criteria.why: expect line 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 not quoted word for word in the builder brief: "`printf 'a\\tb\\n1\\t2\\n' | node bin/csv2json.js --tsv` prints exactly `[{\"a\":\"1\",\""

words-only.why: I compared each check's PASS/FAIL against its expect line. Checks 1–4 ask only for exact output plus a newline, using cmp, and Check 1 also asks for exit 0. Check 5 asks only for exact output with JSON backslash-t escapes. Its first printf actually writes two backslashes, but the brief tells the verifier to confirm the expected file and fix it, so this doesn't make the condition stricter. Check 6 asks for "exit=0" and at least one test that runs bin/csv2json.js with --tsv on tab-containing input and asserts on its output. That matches the line's words and doesn't ask for the test:cli script. Check 7 asks only that README describe --tsv and include an example that uses it. The proof's stricter README form ("node bin/csv2json.js --tsv < file"), the test:cli note, the mutation test, the flag-position check and the parse.js check all sit under "Advisory". No PASS/FAIL condition goes beyond what the words require.

runs-as-written.why: Most commands are fine. The builder's printf/node pipelines, the JS test strings ('[{"a\\tb":"1\\t2"}]\n' gives a literal backslash-t), `npm test`, the grep, and verifier Checks 1–4 and 6 all run correctly as written. Check 5 does not. In `printf '[{"a\\\\tb":"1\\\\t2"}]\n' > /tmp/c5.exp`, the single quotes pass four backslashes to printf, which turns them into two. The expected file then holds `a\\tb`, not `a\tb`, so `cmp` would report a difference even against a correct implementation. The brief admits its escaping may be wrong and offers a node fallback that does work. Still, the primary command, as written, does not produce what it claims, so not every command runs as written.

catches-traps.why:
I checked both must_catch items, and both are handled.

Item 1: The builder brief names test/csv.test.js in its Context section. Step 1 says "Leave src/parse.js unchanged unless you truly need to change it; if you do, the existing parse test must still pass." Step 2 says "Keep the existing CSV cli test." Step 4 makes `npm test` exit 0 and includes a hand check of the no-flag CSV run (`printf 'a,b\n1,2\n'` -> `[{"a":"1","b":"2"}]`). Together these protect the CSV path's tests and behaviour from the --tsv change.

Item 2: Verifier Check 6 runs "`npm test; echo "exit=$?"`", which matches the expect line. Its advisory note says the proof's `npm run test:cli` is wrong because "package.json has only a `test` script", so the verifier should use npm test.

avoids-must-not.why: I checked both must_not items against both briefs, and neither brief does either one. Item 1: in the verifier brief, Check 6's PASS and FAIL depend only on `npm test; echo "exit=$?"` and on reading the tests that grep finds. `npm run test:cli` shows up once, in a section labelled "Advisory (not part of any PASS/FAIL condition)", which only says running it "is informative" if that script exists. So no verdict depends on it. Item 2: the builder brief never asks for a general separator option. It says "do not add --help, --sep or auto-detection" and only adds a `--tsv` check that calls `parse(text, '\t')`. The verifier brief's optional extras don't ask for a --sep or --delimiter option either.

methods-private.why: I compared the builder brief against each verifier check. The builder brief has no PASS/FAIL conditions. It also has none of the verifier's own probes: no `cmp` scripts, no `/tmp/c*.out` files, no `/tmp/c5.exp` escaping check, no `grep -n -- '--tsv' test/*.js` and no mutation test. Step 4 does list hand-run commands with expected outputs, such as `printf 'a\tb\n1\t2\n' | node bin/csv2json.js --tsv; echo "exit=$?"`. These are the exact commands that expect lines 1–5 and their proofs name, which the criterion allows. Step 2's input/output pairs are tests the builder writes itself, built from those same expect-line commands, which is also allowed. "Run `npm test` and make sure it exits 0" is the repository's own test suite and is allowed. So the builder gets the bar but not the checker's methods.
